- Long-established operator, founded in 1993, with modern manufacturing facilities at Vapi and Sarigam, Gujarat
- Diversified product portfolio across FMCG packaging, textbooks, print media and notebooks, serving both domestic and international markets

- Long-established operator, founded in 1993, with modern manufacturing facilities at Vapi and Sarigam, Gujarat
- Diversified product portfolio across FMCG packaging, textbooks, print media and notebooks, serving both domestic and international markets
- Stated focus on cost efficiency, supported by sustained energy-conservation and process-optimisation programmes (turbine upgradation from 5 MW to 6.36 MW, VFD installation, LED conversion, energy-efficient motors and pumps)
- Use of alternate fuels reducing coal dependence — plastic-waste/RDF boiler enhanced from 34.5 TPH to 36 TPH with turbine capacity from 7.6 MW to 7.8 MW, plus a sludge drying system producing boiler fuel with a calorific value of 1000 Kcal/kg
- Positioned in a segment supported by the nationwide ban on single-use plastics and by recyclable, biodegradable paper-based packaging demand
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Expand capacity in the packaging board segment through a new Multilayer Board Plant (Unit VI) of an estimated 1500 TPD at Dahej, Gujarat, expected to enhance manufacturing capacity, improve operational efficiencies and strengthen the Company's industry position
- Fund the Unit VI expansion through a mix of internal accrual and debt, with the Board monitoring project progress
- Source growth capacity cost-effectively by acquiring and relocating a second-hand 4.3 metre deckle board paper machine (2013 make, 1020 TPD) with pulp stock preparation equipment to India
- Reduce energy intensity through continuous energy audits, turbine upgradation, VFDs, LED conversion and replacement of motors and pumps with energy-efficient equipment across all manufacturing units
- Reduce dependence on conventional fuels by expanding use of alternate energy — RDF/plastic-waste boiler enhancement and use of dried paper-waste sludge as boiler fuel to save coal
- Optimise water consumption through mechanical sealing, fresh water recovery, RO plant optimisation and reuse of UF reject and cooling tower blowdown water in top layer pulping
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion is a new Multilayer Board Plant (Unit VI), undertaken during FY 2025-26 as a major expansion initiative to expand capacity in the packaging board segment. The proposed plant carries an estimated installed capacity of 1500 tonnes per day and a projected investment of approximately H1,500 Crores. As part of the project the Company has acquired a 4.3 metre deckle board paper machine (2013 make) with a capacity of 1020 TPD, along with pulp stock preparation equipment, and has initiated dismantling and relocation of the machinery to India. Land acquisition has commenced at Dahej, Gujarat, where the Company plans to acquire approximately 150 acres in multiple tranches. The project is expected to be implemented over approximately three years and will be financed by a mix of internal accrual and debt; upon completion it is expected to enhance manufacturing capacity, improve operational efficiencies and strengthen the Company's position in the industry, with the Board continuing to monitor progress. Separately, within existing units the Company upgraded a 5 MW turbine to 6.36 MW within the same footprint, and enhanced the plastic waste boiler to utilise RDF, raising its capacity from 34.5 TPH to 36 TPH and the associated turbine capacity from 7.6 MW to 7.8 MW, together with a sludge drying system that converts dried paper-waste sludge into boiler fuel.
